result.rationale: Both legs of the score point the same direction: payment evidence shows a genuinely deteriorating pattern (50 DPD on the WT line, a second policy now also 34 DPD, resolution lag worsening 10→14→22 days, notification volume doubling across two policies, and combined exposure nearing the 80M WT limit), and the news leg reflects a matching liquidity-stress narrative (banks reviewing exposure after the company sought longer credit terms amid falling export orders). The High Risk band is therefore well supported by converging payment and news signals. The one caveat is sourcing: the severity-4 story (ILL-001) comes from a single outlet ("Illustrative"); no other trusted article in the book corroborates the lenders'-review story, so while it has substantive text (names two banks, cites falling European retailer orders) rather than being a bare headline, it remains a single-sourced report and should be flagged as such to the underwriter.

concerns.issue: Severity-4 'lenders reviewing exposure' story is reported by only one outlet (Illustrative); find_articles found no corroborating coverage from other trusted sources, so the news-score contribution rests on a single, unconfirmed report (albeit with named detail, not just a headline).
A second policy (TCI-SCF-2026-0001) is now also overdue (34 DPD, INR 9.5M), indicating stress is spreading across funding lines beyond the primary WT policy used as the 'worst_line' in the score.
